card.name: Early colonization history of the Americas
card.fires_on: Small linking words and punctuation in passages about early European arrival in the Americas, just before a colony, settler or Columbus-era term is expected. Typical words are before, at, to, and, and commas.

modes.label: Columbus-era timing
modes.description: Words like before or greeted that come right ahead of Columbus or the voyages.
modes.example: the Chinese visited America more than 70 years<< before>> Columbus.

modes.label: Settlement lists
modes.description: Linking words or commas inside lists of first colonies such as Quebec, Plymouth and Jamestown.
modes.example: First successful French settlements in North America: Port Royal (1606),<< and>> Québec (1609).

modes.label: Arrival in the New World
modes.description: Small words in phrases about Europeans bringing something to the New World.
